summary.intent: Continue improving the monokl code-search tool: land the tokenizer speed fix, then implement member-level blocks (class methods and constructors) using agent teams and workflows while being mindful of model and effort choices.
summary.outcome: Tokenizer fix shipped as PR #64 (ready for review, CI pending), cutting match time from ~49 ms to ~10 ms with all local checks passing. A staged background workflow for member-level blocks was launched (implementer, eval, adversarial review, conditional fix) but had not finished.

repo: Entire is used to publish branches, create trails and open PRs; trails carry findings and gates, and the CLI refuses findings on merged changes so resolved counts show zero after merge.
Release PR #59 gate fails only on 'no reviewers have approved this trail', which needs a human approval.
Local checks include lint, typos, doc-check, cargo deny, machete, drift and changesets; a patch changeset and a decision-log entry (§27) are required for changes like the tokenizer fix.
Decision-log text from agent branches must be merged manually into the spec log.
Default --max-tokens is 20,000 and is now an estimate; --max-results usually binds first (worst measured output ~3,000 tokens).
Eval harness metrics: declaration in top 3, declaration in output, question hits, output size within 25%, speed.
workflow: Staged workflows work best with parallel agents only on disjoint files, in separate worktrees, with an adversarial read-only reviewer that must reproduce findings before a fixer runs.
Scale effort to difficulty: xhigh for the hard implementation, high for review and fix, medium for mechanical eval work.
Record baseline eval numbers before the Rust change lands so regressions can be measured.
Reject bytes/4 as a token estimate because it undercounts by ~17% and could let responses exceed the cap; bytes/3 reads ~11% high and never more than 1% low versus o200k.
Verify agent results independently with your own checks before calling work done.

friction: tiktoken o200k vocabulary construction cost ~40 ms on the first token count, dominating match latency.
CI on PR #64 was still pending at the end of the session.
The CLI refuses findings on merged changes, which makes post-merge resolved counts show zero.
open_items: Wait for the member-blocks workflow to finish, then run own checks on each result and verify the numbers hold.
Implement member-level blocks: class methods and constructors, the innermost-block rule, and the `parent` column.
Four missed eval questions are the main test for member-level blocks.
Reviewer approval for release PR #59 is left to the user.
Merge agents' decision-log text into the spec log.
